A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from Orient Anything to Symmetry-Robust 3D Orientation Estimation. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original orientation-estimation experiments on ShapeNet and ModelNet40 in Tables 1–2, plus qualitative ShapeNet and Objaverse results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds evaluations without test-time augmentation and a single-bench rotation experiment in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: The DGCNN quotient orienter, octahedral loss, 24-way flipper, adaptive prediction sets, and test-time augmentation (TTA) are retained. Appendices B.1–B.2 expand the existing TTA procedure's explanation; disabling TTA is an evaluation variant.

E1.justification: ShapeNet, ModelNet40, Objaverse, and the upright/full-orientation tasks are retained. The added bench-angle sweep probes sensitivity within the existing rotated-shape task rather than expanding the represented domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 6 add the authors' pipeline without TTA as an evaluated comparison variant. The external comparators—Upright-Net and its Random/Oracle full-orientation variants—are unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations disable TTA, and Appendix B.4 introduces a bench rotated about its y-axis in one-degree increments, tracking quotient loss and Chamfer distance between consecutive outputs. Existing data splits, training budgets, and benchmark metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds an ablation isolating TTA's contribution to upright and full-orientation performance. Appendix B.4 and Figure 9 also add a single-shape sensitivity analysis relating output discontinuities to localized prediction errors; neither analysis appears in v2.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the existing plus/minus reporting practice, including for the added row, and conformal calibration is unchanged. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds without-TTA accuracies of 85.3% on ShapeNet and 72.3% on ModelNet40, and Chamfer distance 0.01107 ± 0.04342. The corresponding retained TTA results are 89.2%, 77.7%, and 0.00856 ± 0.0396. New CDF curves and rotation-sweep findings supplement unchanged baseline and APS results.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.2 changes from asserting the stated orientation property for an arbitrary quotient-regression optimizer to asserting existence of a suitable optimizer. This narrows the guarantee while retaining the objective, assumptions, and constructive proof in Appendix A.4; the other propositions and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about symmetry-related regression obstacles, the two-stage solution, state-of-the-art upright estimation, full-orientation recovery, and adaptive prediction sets. The title change does not alter these claims' scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendices B.1–B.2 and B.4 explain how localized discontinuities and error spikes motivate aggregating predictions across rotations to reject outliers. v2 already observed occasional rotation-dependent failures but lacked this developed discontinuity analysis and voting rationale.

D1.justification: Appendices B.1–B.2 make existing TTA implementation details more explicit, including selection by average Problem 3 loss and inverse left-multiplication of augmented flipper predictions. Architecture and training hyperparameters, the code/weights release statement, and embedded access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are retained, including positioning against supporting-base methods, class-specific canonicalization, and equivariant learning. Reference movement across pages does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and many self-references, expands the TTA explanations, adds Appendix B.4, and updates publication and acknowledgment text. Acknowledgments and the impact statement are reordered, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 adds without-TTA curves and revises colors and legends; Tables 1–2 gain a row; and new Figure 9 displays the rotation diagnostic. The original appendix Figures 9–11 are retained as Figures 10–12, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: Tables 1–2 supply previously missing evidence isolating TTA's benefit, the expanded appendix clarifies its implementation, and the narrowed Proposition 3.2 better matches its constructive proof. Appendix B.4 adds useful diagnostic evidence, although Figure 9 labels quotient loss in degrees despite identifying it with the squared L2 objective, leaving its scale unclear. The validation and precision gains outweigh this limited ambiguity.
